conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: I have moderate abdominal pain that started this morning

conversation.speaker: assistant
conversation.text: Can you tell me more about the pain? Where in your abdomen do you feel it?

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: It's in the lower right area

conversation.speaker: assistant
conversation.text: Is the pain constant or does it come and go?

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: It's pretty constant, maybe a 5 or 6 out of 10

conversation.speaker: assistant
conversation.text: Do you have any nausea, vomiting, or fever?

conversation.speaker: caller
conversation.text: No nausea, no vomiting, and no fever that I know of

conversation.speaker: assistant
conversation.text: Are you taking any medications or do you have any medical conditions we should know about?

conversation.speaker: assistant
conversation.text: Thank you. A nurse will review your case and may recommend you get evaluated by a doctor or come in for imaging. Stay close to a phone for a nurse callback.

sbar_structure.situation: 29-year-old female with moderate lower right abdominal pain (5-6/10) onset this morning, constant
sbar_structure.assessment: Lower abdominal pain of unclear etiology; differential includes appendicitis, ovarian pathology, gastroenteritis; requires physical examination and possibly imaging to narrow diagnosis
sbar_structure.recommendation: Nurse review for possible urgent care or ED evaluation; consider abdominal imaging (ultrasound, CT) depending on exam
